why: Courses are nodes and each [course, prerequisite] is a directed edge prerequisite -> course. Every course can be finished exactly when this graph has a topological order, that is, when it has no directed cycle.
hints: Draw each prerequisite as an arrow from the course you take first to the course that needs it. What shape makes finishing impossible?
All courses can be completed iff the directed graph is acyclic. Kahn's algorithm detects this: repeatedly take a course with no unfinished prerequisites.
Build adjacency lists and in-degrees, queue every in-degree-0 course, pop and decrement its successors. If you pop all numCourses courses, return true. O(V + E).
pitfalls: The edge direction is prerequisite -> course; reversing it still detects cycles but be consistent.
Courses with no edges at all still count as completed.
